scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You tap play, and the video starts in a second, even on a shaky connection. Why doesn't it keep buffering?

scenes.name: versions
scenes.text: Before you ever watch it, the video is compressed and saved in several qualities, from one forty four p, up to 4K.

scenes.name: chunks
scenes.text: Each version is cut into small chunks, just a few seconds long.

scenes.name: cdn
scenes.text: Copies are stored on servers close to you, called a CDN, so the data doesn't cross the world every time.

scenes.name: buffer
scenes.text: Your app downloads a few chunks ahead of what you're watching. That buffer covers small hiccups.

scenes.name: adapt
scenes.text: It keeps measuring your speed. If the network slows down, the next chunk comes in lower quality, instead of pausing.

scenes.name: decode
scenes.text: Your phone's chip decodes each chunk back into frames, dozens every second.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Versions, chunks, buffer, switch. Smooth by design. Follow for more on how things really work.
